focus: Frontend files — all 9 frontend files in diff vs spec

findings.summary: font-size: ${t.text.sm} produces invalid CSS — exact repeat of known failure pattern #1
findings.detail: In the Styled.SubjectPreview component, line 308 of the diff reads `font-size: ${t.text.sm};`. Per the pipeline's known failure pattern #1 (motivated by email-subjects-phase-1 impl-round-2), `t.text.sm` is a complete CSS declaration that already includes the `font-size:` property. Using it inside `font-size:` produces `font-size: font-size: 0.875rem;` — invalid CSS that causes the font-size rule to be silently dropped by the browser. The fix is to use `${t.text.sm};` standalone without the `font-size:` prefix.
findings.spec_ref: Known Failure Pattern #1 in pipeline CLAUDE.md

findings.summary: Automation modal's existing-template preview does not display the template's subject
findings.detail: The spec states: 'Automation modal's existing-template preview: show the saved template's subject as-is.' The current diff only adds subject handling for the inline-create-template flow (new state, form input, validation, API call). The existing-template preview section (lines 402-405 of the pre-diff source) still renders only `selectedTemplate.body` via dangerouslySetInnerHTML — no subject display. When a user selects an existing template that has a custom subject, the preview shows only the body. The user cannot see what subject will be sent.
findings.spec_ref: Data flow section: 'Automation modal's existing-template preview: show the saved template's subject as-is.'
findings.fix:
Add subject display above the body in the selectedTemplate preview block, e.g. `{selectedTemplate.subject &&
Subject: {selectedTemplate.subject}
}` before the body div.

findings.summary: Template modal does not repopulate subject with default on validation error
findings.detail: The spec's validation strategy says: 'On submit with a cleared field, fire the standard form-error AND repopulate the field with the rendered default so the user sees the baseline.' BulkMessageModal (diff lines 176-179) and ChannelMessageNew (diff lines 452-455) both repopulate subject with the default when validation fails and subject is empty. ChannelMessageTemplateModal does not — if a user clears the subject and submits, the validation error fires but the field stays blank. The user doesn't see the default they could accept. Similarly, HiringStageAutomationModal's inline template creation lacks this repopulation.
findings.fix: In handleSubmit's else branch, add: if (!subject || subject.trim() === '') { setChannelMessageTemplate(prev => ({...prev, subject: defaultSubject})); }. Same pattern for HiringStageAutomationModal's handleSaveTemplate.

findings.summary: Create-template-from-message uses empty subject instead of the message's actual subject
findings.detail: The fix adds `subject: ""` to the channelMessageTemplate prop passed to ChannelMessageTemplateModal. This means when a user creates a template from a sent message, the template's subject is always set to the default ('{{JobTitle}} at {{OrganizationName}}') regardless of the actual subject used in that message. Post-phase-1, messages will have a stored subject — using `message.subject || ""` would pre-fill the template with the actual subject the user sent. This is not explicitly required by the spec but is a usability gap. The fix is functionally correct (the modal falls back to the default for falsy values), so this is informational only.
findings.spec_ref: N/A — spec does not mention this specific flow
findings.fix: Consider changing `subject: ""` to `subject: message.subject || ""` so templates created from sent messages inherit the actual subject.
